pages.text: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz stated on Thursday that Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa is waiting for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to lose Israel's election before resuming attacks on Druze communities in Syria. parsed.headline: Organised labour in Ghana pushes for higher 2027 base pay

pages.text: Organised labour in Ghana is pushing for a significant increase in the 2027 base pay, arguing that slowing inflation has not translated into lower market prices or restored workers' purchasing power. These negotiations are occurring ahead of the presentation of the 2027 Budget, as the government and labour face pressure to reach an agreement on the new base pay. The current base pay reflects a 9 per cent increase across the Single Spine Salary Structure for the period of January to December 2026.  Dr. Ernest Yorke, President of the Ghana Medical Association (GMA), stated that organised labour will make a strong case for an upward adjustment despite a decline in the rate of inflation. Dr. Yorke explained that lower inflation does not necessarily mean goods and services have become cheaper, but rather that prices are increasing at a slower rate. He noted that workers continue to face high living costs, which have affected their ability to maintain purchasing power. Organised labour is seeking an improved base pay to translate into better salaries, take-home pay, and other emoluments for workers across the country.

parsed.headline: Hamburg court sentences two men for plotting attacks on Jewish leaders for Iran

pages.text: A court in Hamburg, Germany, sentenced two men to several years in prison on Thursday for plotting to target Jewish leaders on behalf of Iran's secret service. Both defendants were found guilty of espionage and attempted murder, according to DW World reporting on the court's findings. One defendant, identified as a 54-year-old Dane with Afghan roots, received a four-and-a-half year sentence. The second defendant, a 43-year-old Afghan man living in Denmark, was sentenced to eight-and-a-half years for acting as the mastermind of the planned attacks. Prosecutors stated the 54-year-old had received orders directly from Iran's al-Quds Brigades, the foreign arm of the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps. He reportedly recruited the 43-year-old to carry out an attack or find a substitute, and tasked him with locating a weapon. The two men had been arrested by Danish authorities in Aarhus last year before being extradited to Germany.

The court found that the pair planned to attack Josef Schuster, the president of the Central Council of Jews in Germany, and Volker Beck, a Green Party politician and president of the German-Israeli society. Additionally, the 54-year-old had reportedly made preparations for an arson attack on a kosher deli located in Berlin.

parsed.headline: IMF projects 3.2% GDP growth for Bangladesh in fiscal year 2026-27

pages.text: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) projects that Bangladesh will experience a gross domestic product (GDP) growth of 3.2 per cent in the 2026-27 fiscal year, a figure that represents the prospect of the country's weakest economic growth in nearly four decades. These projections were unveiled in the IMF's World Economic Outlook during the 2026 annual meetings of the IMF and the World Bank Group in Bangkok. The revised growth forecast is a downgrade from the IMF's July projection of 3.5 per cent and remains significantly below the government's target of 6.5 per cent. Additionally, the IMF projects inflation could climb to 10.9 per cent during this period. During the Bangkok meetings, Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury sought increased support from development partners, specifically the IMF and the World Bank.

Other international development organizations have provided varying projections for the Bangladeshi economy in fiscal year 2027. The World Bank expects economic growth of 3.4 per cent and inflation to remain elevated at 8.6 per cent. The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has forecast 4.0 per cent growth, a decrease from its previous estimate of 4.5 per cent. In its September Asian Development Outlook, the ADB identified persistent inflationary pressures, banking-sector distress, and structural energy shortages as major constraints on economic expansion.

parsed.headline: Israeli military says Hamas commander killed in Gaza City airstrike

pages.text: The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) stated on October 14, 2026, that it killed a Hamas commander during an airstrike in Gaza City on October 13, 2026. The IDF said it took steps to minimize civilian casualties prior to the strike. According to the Israeli military, the commander, identified as Momen Ahmad Salameh Ay, served as an aide to commanders of Hamas’s Gaza Brigade and allegedly held Israeli hostages in Hamas captivity in Gaza City. The IDF further alleged that Ay had recently attempted to restore Hamas’s capabilities and advanced attacks against Israeli soldiers and civilians.

parsed.headline: Explosion hits gas export pipeline in northeastern Syria

pages.text: An explosion struck a gas export pipeline in northeastern Syria on Thursday, sparking a fire, according to reporting by Arab News. The state-owned Syrian Petroleum Co. stated the blast hit the Al-Jabsa gas pipeline in the Al-Arbeidi area of southern Hasakah province, located approximately 60 km from the city of Al-Shaddadi, the Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA) reported. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack, and the extent of the damage or any resulting disruption to gas supplies was not immediately clear. Emergency teams isolated the affected section and shut off valves on both sides of the blast site to contain the fire, while firefighting and security personnel secured the area, SANA reported. This incident marks the fourth attack targeting the country’s energy infrastructure in recent months.

The explosion follows several suspected sabotage incidents involving Syria’s oil and gas infrastructure. On October 7, an oil pipeline near Tal Hamis in Hasakah was damaged in an act of sabotage, according to the Syrian Petroleum Co.; authorities stated those responsible were arrested and referred to the judiciary. On September 28, an explosion struck the Al-Jabsa gas pipeline near Al-Shoula in Deir Ezzor, halting gas supplies to power stations. Authorities attributed that incident to sabotage and restored operations after replacing a damaged section. Additionally, in August, an explosion on the gas export pipeline from the Al-Jabsa plant in Hasakah disrupted supplies to several electricity-generating turbines, an incident for which preliminary investigations indicated deliberate sabotage.
